Hypertrophy · 3× week · M/W/F12-week program

The Foundation Protocol.

Eight weeks with your trainer was the return. That work is done. This is what comes next — building deliberately on the foundation you've already laid.

Frequency
3× / week
Session
45–60 min
Emphasis
Hips · Core · Arms
Schedule
M · W · F
The hip principle

Why hips drive everything else.

Tight hip flexors pull on the lumbar spine. Weak glutes push load onto the right knee. Every session opens with hip prep — it's not extra, it's the foundation that makes everything else work.

01Open the hips
→02Wake the glutes
→03Stabilize the core
→04Then load the body
Weeks 1–4
Build
Build the base. Use trainer-log weights as the floor. Leave 3–4 reps in the tank every set.
Weeks 5–8
Push
Intensity goes up. Loads climb, new patterns challenge you, and working sets stop 1–2 reps shy of failure every time.
Weeks 9–12
Peak
The hardest phase. Last sets go to the edge of failure. Week 12 deloads — then you restart stronger.
Select week

Week 1 — Find your footing.

Phase 1 · Build

Your trainer sessions built the foundation. Week 1 here picks up exactly where those left off — real weights, full range of motion, every set controlled. The only job this week is to groove the new structure.

Week 2 — Load up slightly.

Phase 1 · Build

Same structure as week 1, but bump weight 2.5–5 lb on any movement where last week felt genuinely easy. Add 1–2 reps to the stir-the-pot and dead bug. Side planks go from 20s → 25s.

Week 2 changesSwap flat bench press → Arnold Press on Wednesday (tests shoulder mobility). Add lat pulldown 5 lb. Cable row 25 → 27.5 lb if last week felt comfortable throughout.

Week 3 — Volume uptick.

Phase 1 · Build

Add a 4th set to the two main compound lifts per gym day (RDL and lat pulldown). Introduce a brief 5-min walking pad finisher after the Friday session. Loads climb 2.5–5 lb where form is solid.

Week 3 key changes4 sets on RDL and lat pulldown. Monday: swap cable bicep curl → EZ bar curl (variety for the elbow). Wednesday: add a bodyweight reverse lunge as a superset finish with back extension to start hip stability single-leg work.

Week 4 — Push & test.

Phase 1 · Build

Final week of phase 1. Push a little closer to failure on the last set of each exercise — not all the way there, but leave only 1 rep in the tank on the last set. This gives you a benchmark before phase 2 begins.

Week 4 key changesLast set of each exercise: 1 rep in the tank (not 3). Goblet squat moves to 22.5 lb. Hip thrust increases to 35 lb. Cable row target 30 lb. Add 5-sec pause at the bottom of each RDL. At home: move to 12.5 lb dumbbells on the curl+press.

Week 5 — Phase 2 begins.

Phase 2 · Build

Phase 2 starts now. Working sets stop 1–2 reps shy of failure — you should feel the difference. Loads climb across the board. Reverse lunges get a light DB hold, goblet squat moves to 25 lb, hip thrust to 40 lb.

Phase 2 load targets (starting points)Lat pulldown: 62.5 lb · Cable row: 32.5 lb · Goblet squat: 25 lb · Hip thrust: 40 lb · DB bench: 17.5 lb · Shoulder press: 12.5 lb · Reverse lunge: BW + 5 lb each hand · Back extension: 5 lb all sets · EZ bar curl: add 5 lb to wherever you finished wk 4.

How to progress

When to add weight, when to hold.

If last session you… Next session…
Hit the top of the rep range with 2+ reps still in the tankAdd 2.5–5 lb
Hit the rep range cleanly but had nothing leftSame weight, add 1 rep per set
Missed the bottom of the rep rangeHold the weight, check form
All 3 sets felt genuinely easyJump 5 lb — you were underloaded
Sharp joint pain (not muscle burn)Drop 20%, narrow range of motion, or swap the exercise
Hip, back, or right knee flared upExtend hip prep to 14 min, reduce load 10%

Key principles

  • →Never skip the hip prep. It's the mechanism that keeps your back and right knee quiet. 10–12 minutes. Every session. Non-negotiable.
  • →Protein is still the gap. Aim for 90–100g/day. Muscle built in the gym only shows up if protein supports recovery. Add a scoop to your morning coffee, an extra serving of lentils or beans at dinner.
  • →Glutes do the work, not the back. On every hinge — RDLs, hip thrusts, deadbugs — think "squeeze glutes" before "lift the weight." If you feel it mainly in your lower back, the glutes are asleep.
  • →Right knee tracks over toes. On squats and lunges — if it caves inward, drop the weight and use a mirror. Cue: "push the floor apart" with your feet.
  • →Reassess at week 12. Use your week 11 logged weights as the starting point for cycle 2. You'll be surprised how much higher those numbers are.
